read_side_audit.note: Every row for this epoch, judged by the same rule the collector counts with. A market with a start and no terminal record is one the collector was in the middle of; it counts toward nothing and its artifacts are inventoried, not deleted.

stopped_by: SIGTERM to PID 350548, verified by ps, /proc/350548/cwd and /proc/350548/cmdline as this root's collector before signalling
what_the_corrected_audit_says: Re-read with the corrected verifier the durable material is sound: 4 rows, 4 joined-qualifying, 6 attempts started with 4 finished and 2 left open by the stop, no duplicate starts, no duplicate terminals, and 4 identity-valid latency artifacts. The defect was in the counting, not in what was collected — which is exactly why the counter had to be derived from the durable record rather than maintained beside it.
why_it_cannot_count: The runtime completion counter incremented twice per qualifying market — once when the corpus row landed and again when the terminal attempt record landed — so a --markets 200 run would have stopped at roughly a hundred actual markets.
